scan.summary: This is the OLCC's own producer license for the Bailey Hill grow — the state's authorization to cultivate recreational marijuana at 2210 Bailey Hill Road for the term March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027, at Tier II Indoor with a 10,000 sq ft mature canopy cap. Because it is the agency's document, there is nothing in it to correct or rewrite; what matters is renewing on time, staying inside the conditions printed on it (CTS tracking, worker permits, video retention, reporting ownership/premises changes), and keeping it posted where the public can see it. The one date to run the business off is the renewal cut-off 20 days before expiry, which falls on 2027-02-10.
scan.freshness_note: Issued 2026-03-03 for the current annual term and valid on today's date (2026-09-27), roughly seven months into a twelve-month term. No newer copy is needed until the 2027 renewal is granted; at that point ask for the replacement license for the 2027–2028 term.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on everything read off the face of the document — it is a clean, fully legible one-page licence and all identity facts, conditions and dates are printed verbatim. High confidence that this is a permit and therefore not assessed for gaps. The renewal date of 2027-02-10 is my arithmetic on the document's own '20 days before the expiration date' wording — inferred, not printed; confirm against OLCC's renewal notice in CAMP, which is normally issued about 90 days before expiry. I checked the surveillance rule: OAR 845-025-1450 does require surveillance recordings to be kept a minimum of 90 calendar days, matching Condition 4, and it separately requires off-site backup recordings for a minimum of 30 days — that off-site piece is not mentioned on the licence, so do not treat the licence text as the full statement of the rule. Note that OAR 845-025-1190 is the licence renewal rule and OAR 845-025-1070 covers late renewal fees; I have not verified the current text of either, so treat those citations as my best identification rather than confirmed. I also did not verify whether Ballot Measure 119's labor peace agreement requirement reaches producer licensees (reporting I saw describes it as applying to retailers, processors and laboratories) — worth confirming with OLCC before the 2027 renewal. The signature line on the licence is blank in this copy; that may simply be how the electronic copy prints, but if this is the posted original, get a signed copy.

OREGON LIQUOR AND CANNABIS COMMISSION
9079 SE McLoughlin Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97222
RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA PRODUCER LICENSE
License number: 020-1004763A8B2
Licensee: Evergreen Botanicals, LLC
Trade name: Evergreen Botanicals
Licensed premises: 2210 Bailey Hill Road, Eugene, Oregon 97405
License type: Producer — Tier II, Indoor
Canopy limit: 10,000 square feet mature plant canopy
Original issue date: March 3, 2022
Current term: March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027
Expiration date: March 2, 2027
This license is issued under ORS 475C and the rules of the Commission in OAR chapter 845, division 25, and
authorizes the licensee to produce marijuana at the licensed premises named above, subject to those rules and to the
conditions below.
Conditions of this license:
1. The license is valid only for the premises named above and is not transferable to any other location or person.
2. The license must be renewed annually. A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the
Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date. A licensee that has submitted a complete renewal
application before that date may continue to operate until the Commission acts on it.
3. All marijuana items at the premises must be tracked in the Cannabis Tracking System, and every employee who
handles marijuana items must hold a current marijuana worker permit issued by the Commission.
4. Video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 must be maintained at the premises and recordings kept for at
least 90 days.
5. Any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the persons with a financial interest in the licensee must be
reported to the Commission before it takes effect.
This license must be displayed at the licensed premises where it can be seen by the public.
Issued by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission
Date of issue for the current term: March 3, 2026
Authorized signature: ____________________ Licensing Director
